title: The Old Woman Looks After the Child
subtitle: A Community Raises and Protects Its Future Generations
author: Babi Magil
summary: This proverb teaches that raising children is not only the responsibility of parents but also the responsibility of the entire community. Elders play an important role in guiding, protecting, and passing wisdom to younger generations.

sections.heading: The Proverb
content: “The old woman looks after the child.”

sections.heading: Origin & History
content: This proverb reflects a widespread African community philosophy where children are considered the responsibility of the entire village.
It is connected to the traditional belief that elders are guardians of knowledge, culture, discipline, and moral guidance for younger generations.

sections.heading: Meaning
content: The proverb teaches that children need support from many people, not only their parents.
Elders provide wisdom, stories, discipline, and guidance that help young people grow into responsible adults.
It reminds communities that protecting children means protecting the future.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
content: In many African societies, grandparents and elders played important roles in raising children. They taught traditions, history, respect, and community values.
The relationship between elders and children helped preserve knowledge across generations.

sections.heading: Story
content: In a small village, there was a young boy named Lado whose parents worked far from home during the farming season.
Many people worried that he would lack guidance because his parents were often away.
However, an elderly woman named Mama Nara took care of him. She taught him traditional stories, respect for elders, farming skills, and the importance of helping others.
As Lado grew older, he became known as one of the wisest young people in the village.
One day, someone asked him, 'Who taught you to become the person you are today?'
Lado answered, 'My parents gave me life, but my community gave me wisdom.'
The elders smiled because they knew that every child carries the efforts of many people who helped them grow.
The village continued teaching the next generation the same lesson: a child belongs to everyone.

sections.heading: Life Lessons
content: Children need guidance from the whole community.
Elders carry valuable wisdom.
Protecting children protects the future.
Teaching is a shared responsibility.
Strong communities raise strong generations.

sections.heading: Modern Application
content: This proverb applies to families, schools, and societies today. Children benefit when parents, teachers, mentors, and communities work together.
A supportive environment helps young people develop confidence, knowledge, and good values.
